claims.text: Almost every purchase is a bet on future value: a subscription, a gym membership or a one-off purchase is a bet that it will be used enough for the price of each use to fall to an acceptable number.
claims.quote: Almost every time I buy something, I am buying future value.

claims.text: DellaVigna and Malmendier found gym members on a flat monthly fee of over $70 attend 4.3 times a month, paying more than $17 a visit when a 10-visit pass would have cost $10 a visit.
claims.quote: They pay a price per expected visit of more than $17, even though they could pay $10 per visit using a 10-visit pass.

value.unit: USD paid per expected gym visit

claims.text: Subscriptions are easy to start and tiring to stop: the US FTC's click-to-cancel rule was vacated by a court in July 2025 and the process has started again, and the UK's new subscription rules are due in 2027.
claims.quote: the US Federal Trade Commission's click-to-cancel rule was vacated by a court in July 2025

claims.text: The pain of paying, in Prelec and Loewenstein's 1998 model, plays an important role in consumer self-regulation but is hedonically costly, and consumption already paid for can be enjoyed as if free.
claims.quote: The pain of paying, we argue, plays an important role in consumer self-regulation, but is hedonically costly.

claims.text: In a study Gourville and Soman reported, people who paid in advance for a season of four plays had a no-show rate of 21.5 percent, against under one percent for single-play buyers.
claims.quote: a no-show rate of 21.5 percent

value.unit: percent no-show rate for season-ticket buyers

claims.text: Paying first feels good at use and bad at payment, and quietly decouples the two; paying after the value couples them again, on purpose, at the end.
claims.quote: Paying after the value couples them again, on purpose, at the end.

claims.text: On this site everyone starts with £5.00 of credit; reading uses 10p for a new article read to the end, 5p for an older one, less for other pages, and only as far as you read.
claims.quote: 10p for a new article read to the end, 5p for an older one, less for other pages

value.unit: pence for a new article read to the end

claims.text: The balance can go below zero and stay there; nothing is blocked and nothing nags, and a rating moves the price from free to double or refunds it.
claims.quote: Your balance can go below zero and stay there; nothing is blocked and nothing nags.

claims.text: The £5 payment link has been live on this site since 11 October, with no account and nothing that renews.
claims.quote: which has been live on this site since 11 October, with no account and nothing that renews

claims.text: The point of the negative balance is psychological, not financial: by the time a reader is below zero they have read dozens of articles and the request to pay is connected to them.
claims.quote: The point of the negative balance is psychological, not financial.

claims.text: Wikipedia's fundraising raised US$184.5 million in 2024 to 2025 from 7.7 million donors, an average of about US$10.
claims.quote: in 2024 to 2025, from 7.7 million donors, an average of about US$10

claims.text: A once-a-year request feels heavy because the value is thousands of small moments nobody adds up: the tragedy of the commons applied to your own reading.
claims.quote: a once-a-year request feels heavy, because the value is thousands of small moments that nobody adds up

claims.text: A penny an article for four hundred articles is £4, and easier to give when you can see the four hundred.
claims.quote: A penny an article for four hundred articles is £4

value.unit: GBP for four hundred articles at a penny each

claims.text: The model only works where there is a very large gap between the cost of serving and what you can charge; a business with a real cost per unit cannot let balances run negative for ever.
claims.quote: It only works where there is a very large gap between the cost of serving and what you can charge.

claims.text: This site has no back end, pages are served from a CDN, and the cost of one more reader reading one more article is close to nothing, so even at 10p the margin is very high.
claims.quote: this site has no back end, pages are served from a CDN, and the cost of one more reader reading one more article is close to nothing

claims.text: The model also needs value that adds up visibly; the billing is a side effect of a reading history that is valuable on its own and that the reader can always delete.
claims.quote: The billing is a side effect of that tracking, and the tracking is valuable on its own.

claims.text: Prices should be fair by country, following local purchasing power or wages the way The Economist's Big Mac index measures purchasing power parity.
claims.quote: Prices should follow local purchasing power or wages

claims.text: A reader should be able to see what the money pays for: better articles, fact checks, follow-ups.
claims.quote: A reader should be able to see what the money pays for: better articles, fact checks, follow-ups.

claims.text: In an amusement park experiment, paying what you want for a photo brought about 92 cents each; when half went to charity fewer bought but paid an average of $5.33.
claims.quote: when half of what they paid went to charity, fewer bought, but they paid an average of $5.33

value.unit: USD average payment when half went to charity

claims.text: Verified facts, follow-ups and briefings with every claim checked are things readers, especially commercial ones, choose to pay for separately.
claims.quote: Verified facts are worth more than unverified ones, and to some readers, especially commercial ones, a lot more.

claims.text: The hypotheses H1 to H5 were written before the first payment, two more on personas are in Pay to keep your persona, and the review is on 6 December 2026.
claims.quote: The review is on 6 December 2026.

claims.text: No results yet: the meter has no analytics and the review is in December; nothing here says it works.
claims.quote: The meter has no analytics and the review is in December; nothing here says it works.

claims.text: The balance is notional until you top up: no debt is ever collected, and a negative balance is a number on your screen.
claims.quote: No debt is ever collected; a negative balance is a number on your screen.

claims.text: The studies are about gyms, theatre tickets and photos, not reading; they explain the psychology, not our results.
claims.quote: Gyms, theatre tickets and photos, not reading; they explain the psychology, not our results.

claims.text: Regional prices, a view of where the money goes and the year-in-reading view are proposals, not built yet.
claims.quote: Regional prices, a view of where the money goes and the year-in-reading view are proposals.

claims.text: Wikipedia's figures are its own, from its fundraising report for 2024 to 2025.
claims.quote: Wikipedia's figures are its own.
